Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran a quick internal number-crunch and have two ask areas before I can take anything to procurement: a) can Redwood provide a like-for-like price match vs our incumbent vendor at the same sustained qps profile? and b) if we land on Redwood Dedicated or Private, what are the concrete packaging differences that drive the unit price (reserved GPUs vs consumption, quantization support, and any seat-based licenses)?

I attached a simple workbook with our projected 12-month token/embedding mix — the current vendor gave us a bridge credit and a post-migration uplift to keep latency under 120ms. To be honest, our procurement team prioritizes: predictable spend, fallback during outage, and minimal integration work.

Can you share a concise comparison (cost delta and operational impact) between: Hosted API + reservation credits vs Dedicated reserved pool vs Private VPC? Ideally a one-pager we can circulate to engineering + procurement.

Best,

ForestLytics

Julia — thanks for the clear ask and the workbook. Quick answer up front: yes, we can construct a parity offer, but the practical tradeoffs differ across the three modes you listed. I attached a short "repack options" PDF and a priced scenario in the workbook. High level: 

- Hosted (API) + bridge credits: fastest to start, no infra lift, predictable unit price for token/embedding, but less control over latency tail at very high sustained QPS. Good for pilot and initial go-live.
- Dedicated (reserved pool): predictable throughput and lower per-token cost at scale, SLA-backed latency targets. Migration is mostly a config + traffic cutover, but onboarding engineering is heavier than Hosted.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): lowest operational surface for your security team, gives you isolated networking and KMS/HSM options — higher fixed platform fee and longer lead time for infra provisioning.

Operational differences that affect price: GPU commitment level (how many reserved cards), quantization/precision profile (FP16 vs int8/4), and whether you enable aggressive KV prefix caching (saves tokens but may need integration). We've modeled those knobs in the workbook under the "scenario" tab.

Karthik — can you validate the latency assumptions in the PDF vs the sequence lengths Julia included? Monica — please add an onboarding estimate (weeks, SRE hours) and a one-time professional services line.

Next step: I'll put a consolidated parity sheet together by EOD Wednesday and propose a pilot cadence that limits your risk while keeping cost neutrality for the first 90 days.

Cheers,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Hi Julia — quick technical clarifications inline: 

- Sequence profile: your workbook implies a 1.8x tail compared to median; to hit 120ms p95 on Dedicated we'd recommend an extra 10% commit on GPU to keep headroom for KV cache misses.
- Quantization: int8 gives ~2.1x cost reduction vs FP16 with ~1–3% quality delta on classification tasks; for retraining-heavy workflows FP16 may be safer.
- Fallback strategy: we can route to a cheaper model variant on cost-pressure, but that requires an integration hook (policy endpoint) to be enabled during rollout.

I'll capture these as three concrete deltas in the parity sheet (latency overhead line, quantization sensitivity line, and integration effort line). If you can share a small sample of request traces (anonymized), I can run a short sequence-length distribution check and finalize the GPU sizing.

— Karthik
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Julia / Procurement team — attaching the consolidated parity sheet (tabbed):

- Executive delta table (one-time vs recurring): line items: onboarding PS (one-time), bridge credit (one-time offset), reserved GPU commit (recurring), per-token rate (recurring), observability retention (recurring).
- Proposed commercial: 9-month bridge credit equal to 40% of projected consumption (to match incumbent's near-term economics), then a 12-month committed Dedicated price that achieves ~12% unit-cost advantage vs current list assuming your projected QPS.
- Operational guarantees: 99.95% uptime SLA on Dedicated, can commit to a 120ms p95 latency target for the pilot window if ForestLytics provides anonymized traces (S3 link preferred).
- Packaging note: Private (VPC) option adds a platform fee (~one-time infra setup + monthly manager fee) — numbers included in the workbook.

Next steps: 1) Procurement: confirm acceptance of the 9-month bridge credit structure by Tue 13 Aug; 2) Engineering: upload a 48-hour anonymized trace to our S3 share (I included instructions in the Drive link) so Karthik can finalize GPU sizing; 3) Contract: I'll route a term sheet (clean) with the quoted numbers once procurement confirms the bridge structure.

If that sounds good I'll also add a short fallback clause: automatic routing to Hosted API at a pre-agreed rate for up to 72 hours in the event of capacity disruption. That gives you continuity while we stage Dedicated capacity.

Regards,
